clue.text: Game Field Marshal — a chirpy creature

parts.note: Sir John French was the British Field Marshal who led the army in France in 1914
a cricket is an insect known for its chirping

explanation.surface: A sporting senior officer is described as a cheerful little thing.
explanation.walkthrough: Field Marshal is not a rank to abbreviate but a particular man, Sir John French, commander of the British Expeditionary Force in 1914. The answer is a British garden bat-and-ball pastime where the batter's legs are the wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an example: an informal bat-and-ball pastime played by children in Britain.

clue.text: Only roof over me not standard in any way

indicators.note: not standard means the letters are out of their normal order

explanation.surface: The single roof above the speaker is nowhere near regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not standard' rearranges ONLYROOFOVERME. The phrase is normally heard after 'not', which the clue lends from its indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: used with a negative, it means by any means at all.

clue.text: Starter deficient in powerboat

indicators.note: deficient in its starter means the word lacks its opening letter

parts.note: weight is influence or power, as in throwing your weight about

explanation.surface: A motor launch has a faulty ignition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter deficient in' removes the W of WEIGHT. The single word powerboat has to be split in two: power for the wordplay, boat for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a racing shell rowed by a crew of that number.

clue.text: What they do with old passports to economise

definitions.text: What they do with old passports
definitions.meaning: the passport office clips a piece off a cancelled passport's cover
the idiom for saving effort or money by skimping

explanation.definitionFit: Clipping a piece off a cancelled document's cover is literally what the idiom for skimping describes.

clue.text: In partnership we are to place a restrictive order on plant

parts.note: co- is the prefix meaning jointly, in partnership

indicators.note: we are to place the order, so it is set within the pronoun

parts.note: taken as written
a ban is an order forbidding something

explanation.surface: Business partners plan to impose restrictions on a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are to place' is the insertion signal: the pronoun takes the order inside it. The plant is not a factory but a poisonous wild herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a poisonous water hemlock of marshy ground.

clue.text: Picturesque, like Tennyson's royal verses

definitions.meaning: Tennyson's Arthurian poem cycle is Idylls of the King, so the adjective fits them whimsically

explanation.surface: A scene is as pretty as a laureate's poems about kings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for a charming pastoral scene also describes, playfully, the Arthurian poems Tennyson titled with the related noun.

clue.text: Fabulous horse that's lost in the seaweed

indicators.note: lost tells us the short piece disappears from the longer word

parts.note: a kelpie is the water spirit of Scottish fable that takes the shape of a horse
that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: A marvellous steed has gone missing among the wrack on the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes IE from KELPIE. Fabulous means of fable, not splendid.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large brown marine alga.

clue.text: Faithfully copied, child — he's got animation

parts.note: a tot is a small child
the pronoun, taken without its 's
animation is liveliness, life

explanation.surface: A youngster has made an exact cartoon reproduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: said of a portrait or imitation that matches its subject exactly.

clue.text: Having opened the door, you may be short of money

definitions.text: Having opened the door, you may
definitions.meaning: an open door lets a current of cold air reach you
the British idiom for suffering from a lack of funds

explanation.surface: Showing someone out leaves you hard up.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally noticing cold air come in, and as a British idiom suffering financial hardship.

clue.text: Directly and properly introducing a system

indicators.note: the first piece introduces, so comes before, the two that follow

parts.note: to do something properly is to do it right
a system for doing something is a way of doing it

explanation.surface: Someone brings in a new method straight off and in the correct manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbial synonyms for immediately, without delay.

clue.text: Drunk, man becomes supple

parts.note: lit is slang for intoxicated
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A fellow loosens up physically once he has had a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: both describe a flexible, easily bending body.

clue.text: Go one better than a fête champêtre?

parts.note: champêtre is French for rural, so such a party is held in the open air, out
a fête is a party, and a do is British slang for a party

explanation.surface: Someone tries to throw an even grander garden party than the last.
explanation.walkthrough: A fête champêtre is an open-air entertainment, whimsically an 'out do'; the question mark admits the liberty. The hyphen in the clue as held is only the newspaper's line break.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to surpass someone is to beat what they managed.

clue.text: Do away with about 50 wheels on this

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the thing that wheels are mounted on

indicators.note: about tells us the first piece goes round the Roman numeral

parts.note: to axe something is to abolish it
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An instruction to scrap around fifty wheels fitted to some vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive: it is the rod or spindle on which a vehicle's wheels turn.

clue.text: PM put through the hoop

definitions.meaning: Sir Robert ... was British Prime Minister in the 1830s and 1840s
in croquet, to send another ball through its hoop with your own

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister is given a gruelling ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nineteenth-century British premier's surname is also the croquet verb for knocking another ball through its hoop.

clue.text: English novelist, lived in Australia, ended in Norway

definitions.text: English novelist, lived in Australia, ended in Norway

parts.words: English novelist, lived in Australia, ended in Norway
parts.note: the writer of A Town Like Alice emigrated to Australia, and his full name finished with the surname Norway, which he dropped as a pen name

explanation.surface: A British writer spent time down under and finished his days in Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ended in Norway' is not about where he died: the author's full name had Norway as its last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A biographical description: the author of On the Beach, whose legal surname was dropped for his books.

clue.text: Stretch of river accommodating vessels

indicators.note: accommodating means the river has room inside it for the vessels

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England
pans are cooking vessels

explanation.surface: A length of waterway with room for boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' is the container signal. The vessels look like boats on the water but are kitchen pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a wide stretch of water or land is a broad open area.

clue.text: The holder is to keep the gold

parts.note: to keep something is to have and hold it
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Whoever has the bullion is the one to hang on to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the person who has or owns something.

clue.text: He's rich, bedevilled by treasure

indicators.note: bedevilled means thrown into confusion, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wealthy man is plagued by his own hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bedevilled' jumbles HESRICH. Treasure reads as a noun in the surface but defines as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonyms: to hold something dear.

clue.text: Remedy right for new stage here

indicators.note: right for new means one letter takes the place of the other

parts.note: a nostrum is a quack remedy

explanation.surface: The correct cure for a brand-new theatre platform is found in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' swaps the N of NOSTRUM for R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a raised platform for a speaker or conductor.

clue.text: Fur for the missus in film

definitions.meaning: a white fur used to trim ceremonial robes
the 1942 film about an English housewife in wartime has Mrs and this surname as its title

explanation.surface: A pelt coat for a wife appearing in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A white robe-trimming pelt shares its name with the housewife heroine of a 1942 wartime picture.

clue.text: Three points covered in pay

parts.note: south is a compass point, abbreviated S
the tip of something is its point
the end of a pencil or stick is its point

explanation.surface: A trio of items is included in someone's wages.
explanation.walkthrough: The three points are of different kinds: a compass point, then two words for a sharp extremity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fixed regular salary, as paid to a clergyman or student.

clue.text: Cast in a mould that's diabolic

indicators.note: to mould something is to work it into a new shape

explanation.surface: Metal poured into a form produces something devilish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mould' reshapes CASTINA; cast and mould belong together in the foundry picture, but one is fodder and the other the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: of or like the Devil.

clue.text: Due to get married? Love comes first

indicators.note: comes first tells us this piece goes ahead of the other

parts.note: love is a score of zero in tennis, written O
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A couple are about to marry, but affection is the priority.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: money that is payable is outstanding to someone.

clue.text: The going rate at sea? By no means, they say

indicators.note: they say tells us the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: by no means is an emphatic not

explanation.surface: Someone flatly denies that this is the usual price aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' makes NOT heard as the answer. The going rate is a speed, not a price.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsical description: the unit in which a ship's speed is measured, one nautical mile an hour.

clue.text: Is AGM arranged by letter?

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the annual general meeting is being set up by post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reorders ISAGM. The letter is not post but a character of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the eighteenth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: The appearance of men talking

indicators.note: talking tells us the word is spoken, not written

parts.note: guys is an informal word for men

explanation.surface: How fellows look when they are chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' makes GUYS heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an outward form or semblance.

clue.text: Blow friends up

indicators.note: up means the word is read from bottom to top in a down entry

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: An order to detonate your mates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PALS over. Blow is a noun, a hit, not the verb the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a smack with the open hand.

clue.text: Stand here, as elsewhere you don't see everything

indicators.note: not seeing everything means only part of the neighbouring words is wanted

explanation.surface: From this spot, like anywhere else, your view is incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you don't see everything' takes a run of letters from 'here, as elsewhere'. Stand reads as a command but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a frame that holds up an artist's canvas.

clue.text: Daring turn given twist

indicators.note: to give something a twist is to wrench it into a new shape

explanation.surface: A bold stage act has a surprise added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges TURNGIVEN. Daring looks like an adjective but is the verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: Participle synonyms: having the courage to risk something.

clue.text: Strike in prison about bird given to man (married) produces reconciliation

parts.note: to rap is to hit sharply

indicators.note: about tells us the confined word goes round the three pieces that follow

parts.note: someone in prison is pent, shut up
the roc is the giant bird of the Arabian Nights
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Industrial action in a jail over a girl handed to a husband ends in peace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal, and 'in prison' is an adjective, not a location. Bird in British slang is both a young woman and a prison term, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a restoring of friendly relations, especially between states.
